title: User experience and usability
description: Review or design coherent user journeys, align UI/copy and accessibility, implement requested changes, then independently assess task usability.
intent: Complete the requested journey review, flow design, or scoped UX implementation against project goals and actual evidence. User studies, source changes, and external actions require their requested scope; fewer clicks or polished visuals do not prove usability.

assignments.task: Establish intended users/tasks, current entry-to-outcome journeys, relevant states, project goals, snapshot, coverage, and review/design/implementation boundaries.
Analyze supplied approved user evidence or provide a bounded study plan; distinguish actual observations from assumptions. Do not recruit or contact users.
assignments.when: User evidence is available or a study plan is requested and this role is installed.

assignments.task: Assess approved actual task/funnel/cohort evidence with explicit grain, denominators, and uncertainty; do not fabricate task-success metrics.
assignments.when: Relevant approved data or quantitative interpretation is in scope and this role is installed.

assignments.task: Use completed evidence to assess the existing journey or design the requested bounded flow. Specify entry/exit conditions, transitions, feedback, context persistence, alternatives, and recovery; keep review-only scope read-only.
Align the completed journey specification with project components, visual hierarchy, states, themes, spacing, and responsive behavior.
assignments.when: Visual/component choices are relevant to the requested journey.

assignments.task: Return requested supported labels, instructions, validation, empty/error/success, and recovery copy against the completed flow.
assignments.when: Copy design is requested or material to the scoped flow and this role is installed.

assignments.task: Assess the completed journey requirements and available current interface evidence for keyboard/focus, semantics, assistive use, and applicable accessibility constraints.

Implement only requested scoped UI/flow/content changes or saved artifacts from the accepted brief, preserving user edits and running meaningful checks. A capable domain role may own requested specialist artifacts under the same exclusive-writer rules.
assignments.when: The user requests implementation, fixes, or saved artifacts; review/design in the response alone does not authorize source changes.

assignments.task: Independently walk through representative tasks against the completed current/proposed/changed snapshot; report reproduced barriers, source-supported risks, heuristics, and missing user evidence distinctly.
Check the completed relevant interface or proposal against the declared target, using actual available automation/manual evidence and preserving unverified AT checks.
Review changed behavior, state transitions, preservation/recovery, and actual regression checks without editing.
assignments.when: Source or executable UI behavior changed, or correctness verification is explicitly requested.

assignments.task: Check material task-success, friction, contrast, coverage, or improvement claims against completed evidence; no invented usability metrics.
assignments.when: The deliverable includes consequential quantitative or empirical claims.

assignments.task: Reconcile completed independent findings with the intended journey and project constraints. Return revised recommendations or acceptance gaps; requested source corrections go through the assigned writer and affected checks rerun.

completion: The requested review/design/implementation covers explicit user tasks, transitions, meaningful alternatives, and recovery with evidence and assumptions distinguished.
User evidence precedes journey conclusions, completed flows precede UI/copy alignment, and source writing precedes dependent independent checks.
Observed barriers, source-supported risks, heuristic concerns, visual preferences, accessibility criteria, and unperformed checks remain separate.
Requested changes preserve user context/work and required guardrails; fewer clicks, automation success, or aesthetics are not claimed as proof of user validation.
Optional installed roles are selected only when relevant; unavailable research, browser, analytics, or assistive access remains explicit.
